title: Plate with a hole
summary: A flat plate in tension with a circular hole, meshed freely with extra refinement where the stress concentrates.

steps.title: Start a Model
steps.explain: Same first move as every Model: `model.new` starts an empty one.

steps.title: Choose display units
steps.explain: Millimetres and megapascals suit a steel plate this size.

steps.title: Go 2D: plane stress
steps.explain: This plate is thin compared with its other dimensions and free to bulge through its thickness, which is exactly what plane stress models: a flat Body in the xy plane with a `thickness` that scales stiffness and loads. `model.setIdealisation` has to come before any 2D geometry — a Body's dimension has to match it.

steps.title: Sketch the plate and its hole
steps.explain: `geometry.add` with a `sheet` shape takes a Sketch: an outer loop of line/arc segments, plus hole loops. A hole is a closed ring of arcs about its centre — here four quarter-arcs. Every segment can carry a `tag`, which becomes a face Set (`plate.ymin`, `plate.hole`, …) once the plate is meshed.

steps.title: Define the material
steps.explain: Structural steel: `E` and `nu` are all a linear-elastic solve needs.

steps.title: Assign it
steps.explain: Link the Material to the plate Body.

steps.title: Mesh it freely, refined at the hole
steps.explain: A hole is not a shape the lattice Mesher can follow, so `mesh.set` with `free` triangulates the Sketch instead. `refine` asks for a smaller element size inside a box — here, around the hole, where the stress rises fastest and a coarse mesh would smear the peak. `order: 2` gives curved-edge tri6 elements, which follow the hole's true circle.

steps.title: Fix one edge
steps.explain: Fixing `plate.xmin0` (the tagged left edge) stops the plate translating and rotating, so the only motion left is the stretch the load produces.

steps.title: Pull the other edge
steps.explain: A traction on the opposite edge puts the plate in uniaxial tension — the loading the Kirsch solution below assumes.

steps.title: Add a Step
steps.explain: One static Step, and the Model is complete.

steps.title: Symmetry, and the Kirsch factor
steps.explain: This tutorial fixes one whole edge for simplicity; the accurate way to model a hole in an infinite plate is a quarter model with `constraint.symmetry` on the two cut faces (see the Kirsch quarter-plate example) — a quarter gives the same answer as the full plate at a quarter of the cost.
steps.theory: Kirsch (1898): next to a small circular hole in an infinite plate under uniaxial tension sigma, the stress at the hole's edge, perpendicular to the load, rises to Kt * sigma with Kt = 3 — three times the far-field stress, independent of the hole's radius.
